     3	A campaign connects an authorized request to a bounded goal and existing task
     4	outcomes. It is an opt-in **contract**, not another task queue, a runner, an
     5	approval, or a completion record. This first increment supplies the versioned
     6	schema, pure validation functions and a read-only CLI check. Exploration,
     7	controller execution, cumulative accounting, recovery, goal auditing and
     8	publication integration belong to the dependent autonomy tasks.
     9

    11	python3 cli/go.py validate /path/to/repo --campaign /path/to/contract.json --json
    12	python3 cli/go.py validate /path/to/repo --campaign /path/to/revision-2.json \
    13	  --previous-campaign /path/to/revision-1.json --json
    14	```
    15	
    16	The check reads the canonical `.go` even when invoked in an owned task worktree.
    17	It writes nothing, launches no workers and performs no publication. Without
    18	`--campaign`, existing validation and historical contracts retain their semantics.
    19	The validator does not discover a campaign from a broad vision or an empty queue.
    20	The controller chooses and stores immutable revisions; this increment does not
    21	introduce an on-disk active-campaign pointer or a new state writer.
    22	
    23	## Contract and traceability
    24	
    25	[`campaign-contract.schema.json`](../schemas/campaign-contract.schema.json)
    26	defines `go-workflow.campaign-contract.v1`. All fields are explicit; unknown
    27	fields are rejected. Runtime validation additionally checks relationships and
    28	canonical references that JSON Schema cannot prove.
    29	
    30	| Field | Meaning and validation |
    31	| --- | --- |
    32	| `id`, `project`, `revision`, `previous_sha256` | Project-bound campaign identity; positive revision; revision 1 has no predecessor. Later revisions require the preceding contract, its digest and an increment of exactly one. |
    33	| `intent` | Exact original request text, SHA-256 of its UTF-8 bytes, and source reference. All three remain unchanged across revisions. |
    34	| `goal` | Adopted goal text, non-goals and stable outcome IDs. Refining the goal cannot erase or rewrite existing outcome promises or weaken their required evidence. |
    35	| `goal.outcomes[].task_outcomes` | References to existing `task_id`/`requirement_id` R# pairs with `text_sha256` of the task outcome text. IDs, project/state and text hashes are checked against canonical tasks. No copied outcome statuses or evidence receipts. |
    36	| `goal.outcomes[].required_evidence` | `verification` and `critic` are mandatory. Task release requirements add `release`; required deployment adds `live`. These are proof obligations, never proof that delivery happened. |
    37	| `basis` | Byte hashes of `.go/vision.json` and `.go/architecture-principles.json`, plus exact governing decision IDs. Drift requires review and a new revision. Accepted decisions must still be accepted in the existing decision ledger. |

    42	separators and no NaN. Whitespace in the contract file is immaterial to that
    43	digest. Intent and task outcome hashes use their exact text; basis hashes use
    44	exact file bytes. A revised original request starts a new campaign rather than
    45	rewriting the initial request. New outcomes may be added in a new authorized
    46	revision; old promises remain visible. Remapping a promise to different task R#

    70	## Authority and decisions
    71	
    72	`authority.mode` is `planning` or `execute`. Both require a nonempty
    73	`source_ref`. Planning can retain unmapped outcomes and an empty task allowlist;
    74	it grants no task execution, release or deployment. Execution requires every
    75	adopted outcome to have an existing task mapping and every permitted task to
    76	contribute to an adopted outcome. No wildcard task IDs are accepted.
    77	
    78	Decision dispositions are deliberately distinct:
    79	
    80	| Disposition | Meaning |
    81	| --- | --- |
    82	| `accepted` | Exact existing accepted decision in `.go/decisions/events.jsonl`. At least one accepted reference governs the campaign basis. |
    83	| `delegated` | Routine bounded implementation choice citing the campaign's existing authority source, with explicit bounds and verification gate. It is not a substitute for an accepted governing architecture decision. |
    84	| `proposed` | A candidate choice, with owner and resolution gate. Affected tasks remain ineligible. |
    85	| `unresolved` | An open material choice, with owner and resolution gate. Affected tasks remain ineligible. |

    92	A valid contract can describe blocked work. Callers must first validate the

   102	## Expansion, budgets and delivery bounds
   103	
   104	`authority.expansion` contains separate `research` and `repair` allowances. Each
   105	has `max_tasks`, repository-relative `modify` patterns and adopted `outcome_ids`.
   106	Zero disables that allowance and requires empty bounds. Positive limits require
   107	both a scope and outcome links. Absolute, parent-traversing and platform drive
   108	paths are rejected. The allowance is an upper bound: a future controller must
   109	check the proposed task's actual scope and goal fit, count admissions across
   110	revisions, persist provenance, and admit it in a new contract revision **before**
   111	execution. An unlisted task never becomes executable just because expansion is
   112	allowed. Exhausting the queue never authorizes unrelated work from the vision.
   113	
   114	`authority.models` lists exact model IDs and effort values. There is no default
   115	model, silent fallback or automatic escalation. Execute contracts check each
   116	task's explicit model and optional critic model against that list. Existing
   117	runtime capability/effective-identity checks remain necessary before dispatch.
   118	
   119	`authority.budget` has positive integer `wall_seconds`, `max_tasks` and
   120	`max_attempts`. These are campaign-wide ceilings covering initial work,
   121	research, repair and retries across interruption/resume, not fresh per-task
   122	allowances. The controller must retain consumption; rewriting a contract cannot
   123	reset it. A contract can permit more tasks than can fit the current budget.
   124	Budget exhaustion stops work rather than making the contract structurally
   125	invalid. Metering and enforcement are intentionally not claimed by this build.

   128	sets `allow_push`; an enabled grant requires its own source reference.

   136	All six stop conditions must be declared:
   137	
   138	- `goal_verified`: stop only after actual goal evidence passes the goal audit.
   139	- `budget_exhausted`: stop on the shared campaign budget.
   140	- `no_eligible_tasks`: report remaining outcomes/blockers; do not infer success.
   141	- `authority_required`: retain the unresolved choice or missing grant.
   142	- `unsafe_repository`: preserve dirt and stop unsafe writes.
   143	- `unknown_external_effect`: reconcile the effect before further external writes.

   146	and one owned task worktree at a time. Future runtime work must consume these
